newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent rallies sharply on charts, Iran, NYMEX.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent rallies sharply on charts, Iran, NYMEX.

text.p: IPE Brent crude rose sharply on Monday afternoon on the back of good technical buying after NYMEX opened stronger, traders said.
June Brent was trading at $19.56, 63 cents higher than Friday's close by 1431 GMT while NYMEX's June WTI contract was 86 cents higher at $21.29.
"It's basically WTI leading the market. WTI and the whole complex is up," one trader said. "There's loads of technical buying in the market."

A second trader said: "It's really all technical. The market closed very positively on Friday. I think people are a little bit wary and a little bit surprised it could reach to these levels so quickly because the market was looking overbought."
He said that if it holds these levels, June Brent could hit the $20.00 mark. "There's not a lot of resistance after $19.50," he added.

Some traders said that although June Brent's afternoon rally was technically-led, the market did gain some support from renewed Middle East tension, with the launch of new wargames in Iran in the Gulf on Sunday. Iran is the world third biggest exporter of crude oil.
A top U.S. military commander pledged to defend the strategic Strait of Hormuz against any Iranian threat.
"All this tension helps, doesn't it, but mainly it (June Brent's rally) is generally technical," a trader said.

Most traders said they did not think that the market would gain any strength from a blockade on Monday of the Sullom Voe Brent export terminal by local fishermen. The blockade will not disrupt loadings on Monday with no tankers loading until Tuesday.
Earlier, May gas oil expired at 1100 GMT at $171.75 a tonne, up $1.00 on the day. June was trading $6.00 up at $173.50 at 1431 GMT.
A total of 97,100 tonnes of gas oil will be delivered into the May IPE gas oil contract, an IPE source said on Monday.

Oil dealers had said they expected a much larger volume to be delivered into the contract, possibly between 200,000 and 500,000 tonnes. The contract expired with 971 contracts left open, each representing 100 tonnes of gas oil.
